english.notes:
(i) Harassing a person may include alarming or causing the person distress; a "course of conduct" must involve conduct on at least two occasions and "conduct" includes speech.
(ii) The conduct must have taken place on at least two occasions on or after 16 June 1997.
(iii) In subsection 1(1) the words 'another' and 'other' can be read in the plural. Where the harassment was aimed at two separate neighbours on different occasions (but all the incidents could be shown to be part of the same course of conduct), and both neighbours were named as complainants in a single indictment, that indictment was not duplicitous and was, therefore, valid. There did not have to be a separate indictment (or, by implication, police charge) per complainant (DPP v Dunn 2000)
(iv) Section 5(1) enables the sentencing court to impose a restraining order as well for the protection of the victim.
(v) Incidents in cases of harassment must be so connected in type and in context as to justify the conclusion that they amounted to a course of conduct. See R v Patel [2004] EWCA Crim 3284

other.penalty:
Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
